epochCliff.what: ZkKycRegistry compares a stored grant's epoch against the current epoch at read time, so every grant dies at this instant with no transaction from anyone and nothing warns. getKycStatus goes NOT_GRANTED, canTransfer refuses, and every settlement pair emits SettlementRefused while rounds still cross and prints still go out.
epochCliff.proofsReady: deployments/proofs-live-epoch8.json, three addresses, each verified locally
epochCliff.rootIsEpochIndependent: A credential leaf is Poseidon(credentialId, secret, jurisdiction, tier, validUntilEpoch) and carries no epoch, so the tree published for epoch 7 is bit for bit the tree for epoch 8. publishRoot is write once per epoch and takes any epoch, so the root can go up before anybody needs it.
epochCliff.recovery: script/live/renew-kyc.sh renew 8, after the boundary. Permissionless in msg.sender.
epochCliff.rootForEpoch8Value: 6169089262182662551765430451869477850822369012194942422016362324771265384099, the same value as epoch 7's, because a credential leaf carries no epoch
epochCliff.proofsVerifiedAgainstTheLiveGate: All three epoch 8 proofs agree with every signal the gate pins: passes == 1, credentialRoot == rootForEpoch(8), epoch == 8, registrant == the account, minTier == 3, jurisdictionMask == 255. wouldAccept answers (false, "wrong epoch") and nothing else, which is the clock and not the proof. The nullifier moved with the epoch, so the sybil counter is back to zero of five.
epochCliff.nextGap: Epoch 9 is unpublished. Epoch 8 runs to 2026-09-19 16:33:12 UTC, well past the submission deadline, so it is not on the critical path. renew-kyc.sh prepare 9 when it is.

policy.note: The clock is shared with the superseded stack; the regime and root are not, because Regime.bootstrapSupervisor is single-use and a new engine needs a new cap needs a new regime.
policy.rootPublishes: ten row ceilings, three coalition budgets on rows 13, 14 and 15, and the waiver mask. Fourteen entries.

row13.derivation: the four outcome events crossRound encodes

row15.derivation: the three windows OrderBook partitions a commitment's life into

policy.budgetsWhy: budgetFor(row) answered (0,0,0,0) for every row, which is the unmetered marker, so spentBits was always 0, wouldAfford always true and breakingSize always 0. Three of the five getters DisclosureView exposes were constants and the coalition half of the disclosure model ran in the suite and nowhere else. Rule B is why only three rows can carry a budget; DP-01 is why they did not, and PolicySets.budgetFor is the derivation that answers it.

supersededRoot.published: ten row ceilings and the waiver mask. No coalition budget on any row.

readBackAfterAdopt.row5: budgetFor (0,0,0,0) still. Rule B: an (exact, imm) ceiling admits no budget.
readBackAfterAdopt.note: deployments/client.json disclosure block carries all ten rows, regenerated by `make client`.

actors.note: Two counterparty accounts, keys generated locally and never committed. They exist because a market with one participant is not a market.
actors.sybilBound: ZkKycRegistry.MAX_USES_PER_EPOCH is 5. All three proofs come from one credential, so they share a nullifier and two uses remain in epoch 7.

wiring.regime.supervisor: VolumeCap, so suspension is arithmetic rather than a person
wiring.vault.oracle: PrimeOracle, so postMark is only reachable while the feed is dark
wiring.vault.schedule: CouponSchedule, so every coupon obligation comes from the fixed calendar

market.note: Amounts are in the unit msg.value carries inside the Hedera EVM, which is tinybars: 1 HBAR is 1e8.

feed.note: Deployed 2026-09-07 by script/DeployOracle.s.sol. Two legs. The venue's seated panel publishes LPRC's clean price in USD and the coupon reference rate, because a private bond has no other quote. A seated upstream feed publishes HBAR/USD, because the bond is denominated in USD and every cash figure in this venue is in tinybars, and nothing on chain converted between them before this. The mark is the first divided by the second and RepoVault.markToMarket stores none of it.
feed.decimalsNote: Chainlink's scale, not the venue's. All seven Chainlink feeds on chain 296 answer eight; PrimeOracle._requireEightDecimals refuses anything else rather than normalising. Measured in probes/chainlink-hedera.out.
feed.publishersNote: The deployer and the two live actors from .env.venue-actors. A strict majority, not the whole panel: requiring every seat makes one absent publisher a dark feed. probes/oracle-median.py sweeps where the median leaves the honest range and the boundary is f >= n/2 at every panel size.
feed.cashHeartbeatNote: 26 hours, kept at Chainlink's own 86,400 second heartbeat plus slack even though the seated adapter cannot go quiet. It costs nothing and it binds again the moment a real market feed is seated in its place.
feed.cureWindowNote: An immutable on RepoVault rather than an argument, because markToMarket is permissionless: a caller-chosen window of zero would let anyone call a position and declareDefault it in the next block.

cashFeed.note: HederaRateFeed, our adapter, over Hedera's own exchange rate system contract at 0x168. The rate is the network's; the adapter is 1,323 bytes that put it in Chainlink's AggregatorV3Interface shape so the seat stays swappable.
cashFeed.seatedBy: proposeCashFeed at epoch 515, adopted at 516. The epoch delay was run on chain in two halves rather than short-circuited, so the seat visibly did not move until the epoch turned. script/DeployRateFeed.s.sol is both halves.
cashFeed.whyNotChainlink: Chainlink DOES run HBAR/USD on Hedera, at 0xd4DC5F0a891381D09d6437482a0E4E2dca4ACCAa on testnet and 0x1B9a65b54e36A4f4E3591e4deAAb423C64959Ae0 on mainnet, and this venue tried to seat it. Its proxies are access controlled: a CONTRACT reading one is refused with 'No access' while decimals() answers anyone. All seven feeds, both networks. The seat therefore took a feed it could never price against, the deployment succeeded, and the first markToMarket reverted CashFeedStale. The venue behaved correctly throughout, because a leg it cannot read is dark and dark opens RepoVault.postMark, but the feed was never going to work. Nothing in this repository calls a Chainlink contract; the AggregatorV3Interface is vendored and NOTICE declares it.
cashFeed.evidence: probes/chainlink-hedera.out, read through FeedAccessProbe on chain 296. An eth_call cannot show this: it sets tx.origin to its own from field and the access check passes, which is why every EOA read in that probe's first section succeeds.
cashFeed.divergence: Hedera's rate is council-governed and Chainlink's is aggregated from exchanges, so they do not agree. Measured 2.3 percent apart on 2026-09-07. This is the risk that replaces staleness on this seat; docs/RULEBOOK.md section 4.2 states it.
cashFeed.swappable: CASH_FEED in the deploy scripts, or proposeCashFeed on a live oracle, seats a readable Chainlink aggregator on any chain that permits one. No code changes.

firstRound.note: Three seated publishers, three distinct answers, one permissionless finalize. The prices are deliberately not equal: a round where everyone says the same thing proves the plumbing and nothing about the rule. script/live/publish-mark.sh is the script and prints all three beside the median.
firstRound.median: 100.00 USD per unit of face, 10000000000 at eight decimals
firstRound.markPerUnitTinybar: 124005891271, which is 1240.06 HBAR per unit of face

latestRefresh.note: Published after the scheduled settlement deployment so the UI and permissionless mark-to-market path start with a live feed.
latestRefresh.price: 100.00 USD per unit of face, 10000000000 at eight decimals

coupon.note: Deployed 2026-09-08. CouponSchedule fixes the eight-date ACT/365 calendar. CouponDistributor accepts only fully funded declarations and pays claims in native HTS cash. RepoVault derives manufactured coupon obligations from this calendar and attempts HIP-1215 native scheduling when Hedera reports capacity.

scheduledSettlement.firstCouponCapacity: available when checked before deployment; later quarterly dates use the permissionless manual fallback if Hedera reports no native capacity

superseded.why: The first venue set commitBond to 0.01 ether, meaning 1e16. msg.value inside the Hedera EVM is tinybars, not weibars, so that asked for a hundred million HBAR and every commit reverted WrongBond(1000000, 10000000000000000). The ratio was then measured at two points: 1e18 weibar arrives as 1e8, 5e18 as 5e8. Nothing in src/ was wrong; the deployment parameter was. Regime.bootstrapSupervisor is single-use by design, so the regime, the parameter root and everything seated under them had to be redeployed.
superseded.strandedHold: Hold id 1 on the bond names the superseded engine as escrow and still encumbers 1,000 of the seller's units. Left in place: releasing it needs the escrow, and the seller holds enough besides.

repoVaultBeforeScheduledSettlement.why: RepoVault holds its coupon schedule as an immutable, and MarginWatch holds its vault as one, so adding the fixed coupon calendar and HIP-1215 settlement rail moved both. The oracle, policy, market, journal, bond, and governance stack retain their addresses and state.
repoVaultBeforeScheduledSettlement.stranded: Nothing. The outgoing vault's mirror-node log index was empty before the move, so no repo position or collateral hold required migration.

repoVaultBeforeTheFeed.why: RepoVault holds its oracle and its cure window as immutables, and MarginWatch holds its vault as one, so adding a feed moved both. Nothing else in the venue moved: the parameter root, the regime, the clock, the journal, the engine and the bond all keep their addresses, and script/DeployOracle.s.sol exists rather than DeployVenue precisely so that adding a feed did not spend a governance cycle on a parameter set nobody wanted to change.
repoVaultBeforeTheFeed.stranded: Nothing. The outgoing vault's log index on the mirror node was empty before the move: no repo was ever opened on it, so there is nothing to migrate. Had there been one, the swap would have needed a different shape.

oracleBeforeTheAbiFix.why: Superseded within the hour, and the reason is worth keeping. PrimeOracle.latest() returned a member named `at`, which is a good Solidity name and is also Array.prototype.at. ethers v6 decodes a return tuple into an array-like Result, so `result.at` resolved to the array method, the Repo screen did arithmetic on a function, and the error read 'Cannot convert function to a BigInt' with nothing pointing at the ABI. Renaming it to publishedAt changes the ABI, so the three contracts holding it went up again. HederaRateFeed did not move: it has no such member and the new oracle was pointed at the address already deployed.
oracleBeforeTheAbiFix.fixedForGood: tools/gen-app.mjs now refuses to bundle any ABI whose member name collides with Array.prototype, so this cannot be reintroduced quietly. The check found a second, older instance the same minute: TradingHalt's Resumed event carried `at` too. That one needed no redeploy, because an event topic hashes the parameter types and not their names.

evidence.note: One repo trade, end to end, on testnet. Every number below was read back from the chain.

seamD_refusal.why: ZkKycRegistry answers NOT_GRANTED by the zero value rather than by a branch, and ATS turns that into a revert before any balance is written. The call must carry --from: without it the role check fires first and the refusal says nothing about eligibility.

hold.what: seller createHoldByPartition, escrow = MatchingEngine, no named destination

commits.note: Sealed. What reached the consensus nodes was a 32-byte commitment and a bond, carrying no side, no price and no size.

cross.note: Uniform price in the maximiser interval [95, 105]. Neither side got its own limit, which is the same arithmetic test_theRoundCrossesAndSettles asserts in the suite.
cross.creditNote: Tinybars. Seller: 100 * 1000 proceeds plus the 1,000,000 bond. Buyer: (105 - 100) * 1000 overpayment returned plus the bond.

seamCW.note: The issue landed in epoch 1 and the cross in epoch 4. unverifiedArrivals is zero on both because each recipient holds a live seam D grant, which is the journal's inference working rather than not firing.

receiptBeat.what: The receipt beat, run end to end on chain in disclosure epoch 39, 2026-09-06. Two sealed orders committed and both withdrawn. The first withdrawal emitted Cancelled and DisclosureCharged; the second emitted nothing, refunded the same bond and returned status 1.
receiptBeat.why: DisclosureMeter.spend is Rule A: an exhausted budget withholds the event and never fails the action. Until the budgets were adopted this could not happen on this contract at all, and once they were, it had still only happened in the suite. This is the state no event stream can report, reported: cancelB carries no logs, and spentBits(15, 39) says why.
receiptBeat.bundle: deployments/receipt-beat.json, written by script/live/receipt-beat.sh, which asserts eleven claims about its own run and exits non-zero if any of them fails. All eleven held.
receiptBeat.theTwoCancels: cancelA: status 1, 118,154 gas, two logs, DisclosureCharged(row 15, epoch 39, granularity 1, cost 1, spentAfter 1) and Cancelled. cancelB: status 1, 60,090 gas, zero logs. The gas gap is the mechanism rather than noise: the withheld call writes no meter slot and emits no event, so it costs roughly half.
receiptBeat.theThreeReads: spentBits(15, 39) 0 -> 1 -> 1. wouldAfford(15, pred) true -> false -> false. breakingSize(15, pred) 2 throughout. credit 0 -> 900,000 -> 1,800,000 tinybar, so the silenced cancellation refunded exactly what the audible one did.
receiptBeat.credit: 1,800,000 tinybar left as a credit on the engine for the deployer, claimable with withdraw(). A credit rather than a transfer, following expire: one ledger, one withdraw, no second payout path to audit.
receiptBeat.theWindowThatBitFirst: cancel closes at committedAt + revealDelay, which is 30 seconds. The first attempt put a six-call receipt read between commit and cancel and the window shut mid-run; cancellableUntil caught it and cost a call rather than a transaction. The run is now commit-and-cancel back to back with the reads outside the pairs.
receiptBeat.theTwoStrandedBonds: The aborted attempt left two commitments past their cancel window. forfeit is permissionless and pays the bond to whoever calls it, so nothing was lost: 0x4762be6afcec76ce558d15ff7adb4be95100e543824aa6f3828967f704256ade and 0x15743611292c9fc0417eb28b62f08050332b164d04eaebf8f01b335317495128, 36,476 and 36,500 gas. Both emitted BondForfeited and nothing else, and spentBits(15, e) read zero after both, which is the live form of test_aSweptBondDoesNotSpendTheActivityRow: the recovery path must not spend the row the receipt reports, or a trader's first real cancellation of the epoch would be withheld with nothing on screen to explain it.
receiptBeat.reproduce:
make beat            # plan, sends nothing
make beat MODE=run   # four transactions, 0.002 HBAR in cancel fees
bash script/live/receipt-beat.sh sweep 0xID   # recover a stranded bond

sourcify.note: Every contract listed above, including the four deployed for coupon and scheduled settlement, matched on Sourcify. LPCASH is a native HTS token rather than Solidity bytecode. The verifier URL needs its trailing slash. Forge appends v2 to whatever it is given, so https://sourcify.dev/server becomes https://sourcify.dev/serverv2 and fails with a DNS error that says nothing about the cause.

spend.note: Faucet testnet HBAR. The bond alone was 7.7M gas; the venue was redeployed once because of the tinybar finding, which is most of the difference.

client.note: What a frontend loads. Generated by tools/gen-client.mjs, which only ever sends eth_call and exits non-zero if any of the seven wiring assertions fails.
client.abi: deployments/abi/, 15 files, exported from out/ by script/live/export-abis.sh
client.holdRail: IHoldByPartition carries six entries. getHeldAmountForByPartition was added 2026-09-06 as row 12 of the docs/ats-seams.md call list, and it is the first row on that list no contract of ours calls. balanceOfByPartition excludes held units, so a position needs both numbers: 2,000 free and 1,000 held for the seller, measured.
